newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in dull late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in dull late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Monday, dealers said.

"It's a dull market. I think people are just squaring positions ahead of a public holiday on Wednesday," one European bank dealer said, adding that the underlying tone seemed to be in favour of the dollar.
He said operators tended to stay long on the dollar after the rupiah was sent reeling last week on unfounded rumours about the health of President Suharto.
Dealers said the market had stabilised and swap rates indicated some easing on slightly excess liquidity.
Spot rupiah was at 2,405.00/05.25 at 0930 GMT against an opening of 2,405.0/06.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,404.50/04.75 and 2,404.50/04.85, respectively.
"The tone looks biddish on dollars," the European dealer said. He said some operators tried to push the dollar up after the central bank surprisingly raised its fixing by two points.
"But there were sufficient counters which kept the rupiah stable around the morning level," he said.
Bank Indonesia depreciated the rupiah to 2,397/2,589 for the intervention band and to 2,397/2,445 for the conversion band.
One dealer said six-month swap rose briefly at midday but edged down later on the back of ample liquidity.
He said the focus was more on short-term, one- and two-week, swaps due to the upcoming new reserve rate.
One- and two-week swaps were at 2.4/2.6 and 5.25/5.75.
One-month swaps were at 12.50/12.75, two at 24.0/25.0, three at 35.0/35.5 and six at 71.0/72.0 points.
